title: The Gunthorpe Fallen and Lancaster R5703
memorial_details: Memorial is a wooden post with two simple metal plaques, one dedicated to the Gunthorpe Fallen 1914-1918 and the second dedicated to the crew of a bomber that crashed nearby with an etching of a Lancaster. In the photo red bows are tied round the post
inscription: Plaque 1: Riverside Landscape/ Planted in memory of/ THE GUNTHORPE FALLEN/1914-1918 Plaque 2: In Memory of/ the Bomber Crew/ who died in the/ Parish of Gunthorpe

sources.title: Facebook post by Dave Sanderson (RAF Bomber Command Memorials group) — identifies riverside memorial near Gunthorpe, River Trent, Nottinghamshire

narrative: Lancaster R5703 crashed in the parish of Gunthorpe, Nottinghamshire. The combined riverside memorial — a wooden post bearing two metal plaques — commemorates both the Gunthorpe Fallen of 1914–1918 and the bomber crew who died nearby. The second plaque shows an etching of a Lancaster. Further details of the aircraft's unit, date of loss, crew and cause are not yet established. A Facebook post by Dave Sanderson in the RAF Bomber Command Memorials group records the riverside memorial; the aircraft type was not stated in the post (a Lancaster is depicted in the etching on the plaque and named in the site's title).
